hero.headline: Aged stock has risen to 14.7% of the value on the shelf, 1.8 points higher than on 14 August
hero.narrative: Counted in units rather than money the picture is the same: 14.9% of units were nine months old or more on 14 August, and 18.1% are now. Totals are not compared between the two dates, because stock value is worked out differently on each of them. Shares are, because a share compares two figures taken on the same day. USD 91K of stock is more than two years old, 1.6% of all stock value as at 2026-08-23. This is the most likely write-off candidate and is reported separately from the 12-24 month band.

lanes.value_note: ST5 holds the same quantity of stock on both dates (79,838 units) but its value has moved from 0.78 to 0.21 per unit. Stock that did not move cannot change in worth, so the way stock value is calculated has changed between the two dates. Value figures are therefore not compared here.

lanes.title: Since yesterday's reading
lanes.sub: compared with the position this report kept on its last run
lanes.reason: The dashboard still reports the same position date as the last copy kept, so there is no movement to report. Figures describe that position only.

change.caption: Ageing is judged on shares rather than totals, because a share compares two figures taken on the same day and is not affected by anything that rescales them.

caveats: This assumes each sale takes the oldest stock first, which the source data does not guarantee. Read it as 'this division is slow to turn over', not as a promise about the next 30 days.
25% of recorded daily sales belong to products that are not mapped to a division, so they are not counted in any row below. The divisions shown may clear slightly faster than these figures suggest.

categories.note: Each category is measured against its own stock, so a small category with a bad ratio still counts. The list below is ordered by how much money is stuck, not by the percentage, so the biggest problems come first. 30% is a review line that can be moved.

stuck.note: The ageing risk score runs from 0 (healthy) to -100 (worst) and is calculated inside the source report. Stock value in this table comes from the stock-status table, which is on a different basis from the headline stock value above, so the two are not added together.

ST5 holds the same quantity of stock on both dates (79,838 units) but its value has moved from 0.78 to 0.21 per unit.
